newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Japanese leader to visit Australia April 28, 29.
newsitem.headline: Japanese leader to visit Australia April 28, 29.

text.p: Australian on Thursday confirmed Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto would visit on April 28 and 29.

Prime Minister John Howard, who travelled to Japan in September on his first official overseas visit as prime minister, said Hashimoto's visit reflected the importance Canberra and Tokyo attached to warm relations.
"Mr Hashimoto's acceptance of my invitation reflects the importance we both attach to maintaining the closest possible cooperation between us and our two countries," Howard said in a statement.
"Japan is a close friend of Australia's and a highly-valued partner in regional and international affairs.
"Mr Hashimoto's visit provides a welcome opportunity to discuss how we can best promote our economic and political partnership and our cooperation in regional affairs."
Hashimoto will visit Canberra and Sydney.
Japan is Australia's major trading partner and Australia is one of the few countries with which Japan has a trade deficit.
Australian exports to Japan, mainly resource and farm products, were worth A$16.42 billion (US$12.32 billion) in fiscal 1995/96, compared with imports of A$10.82 billion.
The two countries have also been closely allied in pushing the free trade agenda within the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, grouping 18 Pacific Rim economies.
